Confirmed, and fixed at the head of this pull request. The restore took back the path and the bytecode switches but not the module cache, so `proofbundle` and `proofbundle._wire_b64` stayed loaded from the judged checkout.

## Reproduced

Measured now with the two cases that pin it, `test_a_module_from_the_judged_path_leaves_and_one_from_before_stays` and `test_a_measurement_in_a_fresh_interpreter_leaves_no_module_of_the_judged_tree`, run once against the scripts of the reviewed commit `9b02c1fa24409e58a7f71ece30f70fd96aebd6f6` and once against those of head `cc6f0b493a39aa6ad7288a28595f5e497f612812`, the test file being the same in both runs. Both fail with the reviewed scripts and pass with the head.

## Fix

Fixed in `dd27add5071ed1423d415a49d046141bda277e16`. `_importzustand` in both verifiers records `sys.modules` on entry and removes, on exit, what the call loaded for the first time from a path it put on `sys.path`, while a module first loaded from a path that was there before stays. The two cases above pass at head `cc6f0b493a39aa6ad7288a28595f5e497f612812`, the second one end to end in a fresh interpreter with the judged `proofbundle` loaded, as a marker file proves.

## Not covered

The restore covers the import state, the path, the two bytecode switches and the module cache. Code from the judged tree runs in-process during the measurement and can change other process state, which this restore does not claim to undo.

Commit measured `cc6f0b493a39aa6ad7288a28595f5e497f612812`
